title: Establishment of a spectral tissue library and perfusion imaging using hyperspectral imaging (HSI) in intracranial vascular and neoplastic pathologies
summary:
The intraoperative differentiation between tumor tissue and healthy tissue in neurosurgery relies heavily on modern intraoperative imaging techniques. In certain cases, fluorescence dyes or ultrasound reach their limitations, creating a need to explore hyperspectral imaging (HSI) as a minimally invasive and contrast-agent-free imaging method. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is an innovative technique that uses light to analyze tissue in great detail. Unlike conventional cameras that capture only a few colors (such as red, green, and blue), a hyperspectral camera can record hundreds of different wavelengths simultaneously. This generates "spectra," which serve as an optical fingerprint of the tissue.

In neurosurgery, HSI is used to visualize the properties of brain tissue in real time during surgery. Only in vivo measurements are performed — meaning the imaging is done directly on the patient without removing or altering any tissue. Based on these measurements, no tissue removal (resection) is performed at this stage. The goal is to use the collected HSI data to better detect and later more precisely characterize differences between healthy and pathological tissue (e.g., tumors).

In the long term, this technology could help make surgeries even safer and more precise. Currently, however, HSI primarily serves to collect data and to improve understanding of how different tissue types can be optically distinguished.
conditions: Meningiomas, Gliomas, Brain metastases, Cerebral aneurysms, Arteriovenous malformations, Vestibular schwannoma, Cavernoma

interventions.name: Intraoperative  in-vivo visualization of neoplastic or vascular neurosurgical pathologies using HSI.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Cranial neoplastic or vascular disease
Exclusion criteria:
Patients incapable of giving informed consent (lack of voluntary agreement).
Pregnant or breastfeeding women, and individuals planning pregnancy (considered particularly vulnerable groups).
Children and adolescents under 18 years of age (considered particularly vulnerable population).
